pages.text: "I'll play again after dinner!" Mina left the top and wooden dolls in the yard and went inside. The low river had left soil dry right to the yard's edge. The toy basket under the platform was empty.
After eating, Mina's eyes began closing. Sonu said, "My doll is outside, too." "We can get it tomorrow morning." Mina crawled under the quilt.
Coming outside in the morning, Mina stopped. A goat stood on the top. "My top!" One side had cracked.
Sonu's wooden doll was missing, too—not under the platform or behind the tub. Sonu's mouth drooped. "You didn't put it away..." Mina could say nothing.
Mom put the empty basket in the yard's middle. "Gather all the scattered things first." Mina and Sonu walked around, collecting them one by one.
Game stones lay by the wall, the top's string under the platform. Mina put each in the basket. In, in, in. In a singsong voice, Mina said, "After Playing, Into the Basket!"
Lifting a dry-grass pile revealed the buried doll. "Mine!" Sonu hugged it in both hands. "Tidying made the missing thing appear."
Mom bound the cracked top tightly with twine. "Let's fix it together tomorrow." Mina carefully put it in the basket.
That evening, Mina looked around the yard. "Sonu, did you get your doll?" Mina slid the basket beneath the platform.
In the morning, the goat crossed the empty yard. Mom stroked Mina's back. "Are the toys safe?" "Yes! All in the basket!"
